subject: physics_2
question_text: Define focal length of a concave mirror. Prove that the radius of curvature of a concave mirror is double its focal length.

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed p.11 — Section B, 4 marks. The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. The figure carries ZERO marks because the printed question does not say 'draw a neat labelled diagram' — a teacher may well award a diagram mark here, and that is one of the things to confirm. Hand-checked physically: with M the point of incidence, C the centre of curvature, D the foot of the perpendicular from M, tan θ = MD/CD and tan 2θ = MD/FD; for a paraxial ray θ is small, D lies close to P, and CD → R, FD → f give 2/R = 1/f, that is R = 2f. The exterior-angle result angle MFD = 2θ follows from angle MCF = θ and angle CMF = θ (CM is the normal, so the angles of incidence and reflection are both θ).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

The distance between the pole P of the

steps.margin_note: First mark. Measure f from the POLE, not from the edge of the mirror.
steps.why: The focus is defined by one special beam, the beam parallel to the axis. Everything measured on a mirror is measured from the pole, so the focal length is the pole-to-focus distance.
common_mistakes: Measuring f from the centre of curvature. It is measured from the pole.
Defining F by any converging beam. Only the beam parallel to the axis defines the principal focus.

recall.must_convey: That the focal length is the distance between the pole and the principal focus, where rays parallel to the axis meet after reflection.

reject: the radius of curvature is twice the focal length

steps.memory_tip: P to F is f. Every mirror distance starts at the pole.

steps.label: Ray diagram
steps.margin_note: A ray parallel to the axis meets the mirror at M. CM is the normal, MD is the perpendicular from M on the axis.
steps.why: The figure fixes the two triangles the proof uses: MCD gives the angle at the centre of curvature, MFD gives the angle at the focus. Nothing else in the proof needs a picture.
common_mistakes: Drawing the normal at M perpendicular to the mirror surface by eye. The normal is the line MC, joining M to the centre of curvature.

Then angle MCD = θ and angle MFD = 2θ.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Both triangles share the same side MD — that is what lets them be combined.
steps.why: MFD is the exterior angle of triangle MCF, and the two interior opposite angles are both θ, so it equals 2θ. The shared side MD is the bridge: it appears in both tangents and cancels later.
common_mistakes: Writing angle MFD = θ. It is the exterior angle and equals 2θ.
Using the wrong sides in the tangent. MD is opposite the angle in both triangles.

recall.must_convey: That angle MCD = θ and angle MFD = 2θ, giving tan θ = MD/CD and tan 2θ = MD/FD.

steps.margin_note: Third mark. Two approximations, both stated: small angle, and D close to P.
steps.why: Without the paraxial assumption D is not at P and the result is not exact. Stating both approximations is what makes the proof honest, and each one is a separate thing the examiner looks for.
common_mistakes: Replacing CD by R without saying that D is close to P.

steps.label: R = 2f
lines: The radius of curvature of a concave mirror
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Cancel MD and finish with the sentence in words.
steps.why: MD is the same length in both expressions, so it cancels and leaves a relation between R and f alone. That cancellation is the whole point of choosing the two triangles that share MD.
common_mistakes: Writing f = 2R. The focal length is the SMALLER of the two.
Leaving the answer as 2/R = 1/f without inverting to R = 2f.

recall.must_convey: That MD cancels to give 2/R = 1/f, so R = 2f.

steps.memory_tip: The focus sits halfway between the pole and the centre of curvature. R = 2f is that sentence in symbols.

insider_note: Four moves: define f, set up the two triangles, make both angles small, cancel MD. The figure is what makes the two triangles obvious.
